   MEMORANDUM

  Agenda Item #:_1_
  Meeting Date: November 14, 2017

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  ANTON DAHLERBRUCH, CITY MANAGER /s/

SUBJECT: DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF ESTABLISHING A
  FINANCE ADVISORY COMMITTEE FOR CITYWIDE FISCAL
  MATTERS

DATE:  NOVEMBER 14, 2017

ISSUE/PURPOSE

Shall the City Council create a Finance Advisory Committee addressing citywide fiscal
matters?

BACKGROUND

At its meeting of October 24, 2017, the City Council discussed whether or not to establish a
citywide Finance Advisory Committee. The preliminary conclusions of the City Council were
as follows:

1. A citywide Finance Advisory Committee should be established.
2. A Finance Advisory Committee should be comprised of 5 individuals, ideally with a
  financial background.

With the role and scope, term, duration and logistics, and resource support for the Committee
undetermined, the City Council continued the discussion of this topic to November 14, 2017
at 6:00 p.m.

DISCUSSION

As presented at the meeting of October 24, 2017, below are several remaining questions that
are intended to prompt discussion for establishing the role and scope; term, duration, and
logistics; and resources for a Finance Advisory Committee.

  Page 1 of 4
   What will be the purpose (role and scope) of a Finance Advisory Committee?

  1.  Decision making authority or advisory
  2.  Role in reference to financial and budget reports
  3.  Role in reference to fiscal and operating policies
  4.  Role in reference to day-to-day operations (e.g., new appropriations)
  5.  Role in reference to financial planning

  What will be the term of Committee members, duration of the Committee and other
  meeting logistics?

  6. During the year, should the committee meet monthly, quarterly, a minimum number of
  times (e.g., 2 corresponding to a review of the budget and annual financial report), or
  maximum number of times?
  7. Initially, should the Committee “sunset” at a specific date for the City Council to
  conduct a formal review of it?
  8. What should be the term(s) of Committee members? Note: The City Council approves
  a bi-annual budget; the next budget will be for July 1, 2018 to June 30, 2020.

  What resources will be appropriated to support the Committee?

  A City Council appointed Finance Advisory Committee would be subject to the Ralph M.
  Brown Act. As such, meeting would require preparation and posting of the agenda and
  associated staff reports and materials, appropriate noticing of public meetings and hearings,
  and opportunities for public input consistent with all other commissions and committees.
  It is recommended that the meetings be webcast (recording is approximately
  $275/meeting).

  For cost savings, efficiency, and document management, the City strives to be paperless
  and retain records in digital format. For City Council, Commission and Committee
  meetings, this is supported by issuing Ipads (approximate cost of $500 per device). City-
  issued (in contrast to privately owned devices) Ipads are further recommended for the
  retention and production of public records. The City also, only, supports the functionality
  of and takes responsibility for City-issued equipment. Ipads will be particularly helpful for
  a Finance Advisory Committee, as financial documents are quite lengthy. For these
  reasons, City-issued Ipads are recommended.

  Part-time hours are necessary to avail the existing staff with the time 1 necessary to support
  the committee (conservatively estimated to be $35 per hour for an estimated average of
  approximately 8 hours per week). The cost is estimated to be approximately $7,280.
  Current staffing cannot support the time commitment necessary for a committee consisting
  of training committee members, research, report preparation, agenda preparation, posting
  and noticing, responding to inquiries, and responding to direction from meetings. The
  Finance Department consists of a Finance Director, Senior Accountant, and two Finance

1
  Staff time is necessary for preparing agenda materials, posting and noticing, attendance at meetings, and research and
report assignments from the committee.

  Page 2 of 4
   Technicians. The four are fully stretched sustaining current operations and have a work
  plan encompassing numerous accounting, audit, budget, and treasury responsibilities. It is
  recommended that funding be budgeted for part-time hours.

  Additionally, the estimated cost to support the proposed Committee does not include the
  potential for consulting services for, for example, developing a facility-needs master plan
  schedule and budget like the one referenced as being developed by the Palos Verdes Golf
  Club.

  Potential Description of a Finance Advisory Committee

  At the October 24, 2017 meeting, it was mentioned that the description of the Rancho Palos
  Verdes Finance Advisory Committee (here), without the reference to economic development,
  may be consistent with the City Council’s intended goals. As such, it is provided below.

  The mission of the Finance Advisory Committee shall be to provide citizen input to the
  City Council regarding financial matters of the City of [Palos Verdes Estates]. The
  Committee shall review short and long-term financial information of the City and other
  financial issues as assigned by the City Council. The Committee will serve to advise the
  City Council regarding the City's financial condition.

  FISCAL IMPACT

  The initial fiscal impact of a committee is estimated to be $275 per meeting for videotaping
  ($1,100 annually if meetings are, for example, quarterly), approximately $500 per member
  for an IPad ($2,500), and approximately $7,280 for the hourly costs for a part-time staff
  person ($35 per hour for 8 hours per week) 2. The total cost of the committee is projected and
  estimated to be $8,380 annually plus the one-time cost of $2,500.

  NOTIFICATION

  This item was noticed consistent with requirements and according to standard practice.

  ALTERNATIVES

  The alternatives available to the City Council include but are not limited to:

  A. Provide staff with information describing a Finance Advisory Committee and direct the
  preparation of an Ordinance.
  B. Continue discussion to another meeting.
  C. Request additional information.
  D. Provide alternative direction.
  E. Decline to act.

2
 Part-time support is necessary because existing staff are at capacity with a full range of finance and administrative
functions.

  Page 3 of 4
 CONCLUSION/RECOMMENDATION

For establishing a committee and subsequent appointment of committee members, the
following represents a timeline. It may be different based on the City Council’s schedule of
calendared meetings:

  Day 1 -  Post notice of Public Hearing
  Day 11 (City Council Meeting) -  Public Hearing for Introduction of Ordinance
  Day 24 City Council Meeting) -  Adoption of Ordinance
  Day 54 -  Ordinance becomes effective

  No earlier than:
  After Day 24 -  Public application period
  After Day 38  Applicant interviews
  After Day 48 -  City Council announcement of committee members
  After Day 60 -  First meeting / orientation

It is recommended that the City Council consider provide direction to staff.

  1  001
   PVrrg Recommendations
  Palos Verdes Citizens Financial Advisory Committee

The following document represents PVrrg recommendations regarding the
concept paper drafted by the City Manager. For each section outlined by
the City Manager below, PVrrg recommendations follow in red.

“Citywide Finance Advisory Committee Concept Paper”

Purpose:

  The Finance Advisory Committee shall:
  •  Provide advice to the City Council regarding short and
  long range financial planning and funding.
  •  Review the City’s financial documents and statements
  (specifically, the budget and annual financial
  report).
  •  Make recommendations to the City Council regarding
  financial and budgetary policy.

PVrrg Recommendation:

  • Provide advice and recommendations to the City Council
  regarding short and long range issues including financial
  planning.
  • Review the financial plans and performance relating to
  budgeted and actual revenues and expenditures on a
  quarterly and annual basis, as well as periodically review
  the long range plan.
  • Review and report on other finance related issues as assigned
  by the City Council.
  • Make recommendations to the City Council regarding
  financial and budgetary policies and issues as
  appropriate.
  • NOT responsible for selection of auditors nor performing
  audits.

  PVrrg recommends adding the following:

  002
 Guiding Principles:
  • Conduct: The Committee Members will conduct themselves in
  accordance with the highest ethical standards.
  • Independence: This Committee is answerable to the citizens of
  Palos Verdes Estates and their elected representatives.
  • Transparency: All meetings will be properly noticed and open to
  the public, and all meeting materials will be made available.

Composition:
  The Finance Advisory Committee shall be comprised of 5 residents. All members
  shall be residents of Palos Verdes Estates. Members of Finance Advisory Committee
  shall be appointed by the City Council.
  For the initial appointments, three positions will serve a 15-month term and two
  position will serve a 27 month term ending on June 30, 2019 and June 30, 2020,
  respectively. Subsequent appointments to the Committee shall be for two years
  concurrent with the City’s regular appointment process. Terms will be staggered.
  Annually, the Mayor will appoint the Chair and Vice Chair of the Finance Advisory
  Committee.

PVrrg Recommendation:

  The Finance Advisory Committee shall be comprised of 5 PVE residents,
  one of whom is the City Treasurer. All members shall have appropriate
  experience/background in finance and/or financial management.

  Finance Advisory Committee candidates shall be preliminarily
  interviewed and their suitability assessed by the City Treasurer.
  Candidates deemed to be qualified will be presented to the City Council
  for review and final selection.

  For the initial appointments, two positions will serve a 16 month term and
  two positions will serve a 28 month term, ending on June 30, 2019 and
  June 30, 2020 respectively. Members whose terms have expired may re-
  apply for a second term.

  Subsequent appointments to the Committee shall be for two years,
  concurrent with the City’s regular appointment process. Terms will be
  staggered.

  003
 Chair Person:

The City Treasurer shall serve as the Chair and shall appoint the Vice
Chair. The Chair and Vice Chair will determine meeting agendas
consistent with Committee charter as well as Council needs and requests.

Duration:
The Finance Advisory Committee shall be established March 1, 2018 and conclude
June 30, 2022 unless, by action of the City Council, the Committee’s term is
extended.

PVrrg recommendation:

The Finance Advisory Committee shall be established no later than March
1, 2018 and be continued until at least June 30, 2022. Prior to June 30,
2022 the City Council will review and determine whether to continue,
modify or conclude the Committee.

Meetings:
All meetings of the Finance Advisory Committee shall be subject to State and Local
laws and ordinances including the Ralph M. Brown Act.
The Finance Advisory Committee will meet at least one (1) time per year between
April 1 and June 30 to review and assess the bi-annual budget, and at least one (1)
time per year to review and assess the City’s annual financial report for no less than a
total of two (2) times per year. The Committee will meet no more than 4 times a year.
If the committee meets 4x per year, $1,100 will be budgeted for video recording of
meetings.
Meetings will be held in the City Council Chambers on Mondays at 7:30 p.m.

PVrrg recommendation:

The Finance Advisory Committee shall meet quarterly and may meet
more frequently as requested and approved by the City Council.

Other:
Committee members will be provided an Ipad for agenda materials. $2,500 will be
budgeted for the acquisition of the Ipads.
Part-time staffing will be necessary for staff to support a committee. Approximately

  004
   $7,280 for the hourly costs of a part-time staff person ($35 per hour for 8 hours per
  week) will be budgeted.

  PVrrg recommendation:

  The need for staff support will be assessed and determined by the
  Committee in consultation with City staff after the Committee is formed
  and begins meeting. In any case, the level of staff support is not expected
  to exceed an average of 2 hours per week since it is anticipated that the
  necessary materials will be prepared by the City in the normal course of
  its financial administration.

Respectfully submitted November 9, 2017 by the PVrrg Steering Committee:

John Harbison, Rose Ramsay, Michael Thiel, Jenene Wilson
